name: manual_fcfa58
claim: When a factory function's default is tuned for one calling contract (e.g. ssrf_session()'s max_redirects=0 for standalone 'refuse redirects entirely' usage) and the SAME factory is reused internally by a second function with a genuinely different contract (ssrf_request()'s own manual per-hop redirect loop, which needs the underlying requests.Session to NOT eagerly enforce a redirect ceiling), the second function must not assume the shared factory's defaults are compatible with its own needs -- requests.Session.send()'s internal precomputation of resp._next (via resolve_redirects(..., yield_requests=True)) raises TooManyRedirects on literally the first redirect when session.max_redirects=0, regardless of the per-call allow_redirects=False kwarg, silently making the caller's own manual redirect-handling loop unreachable for any real HTTP response
conditions: requests Session max_redirects shared factory contract mismatch

decisions.notes: ssrf_request() in src/utils/ssrf_pinned_adapter.py creates its session via ssrf_session(), which sets session.max_redirects=0 for its own documented direct-usage contract ('redirects are refused'). But ssrf_request()'s own while-loop (per-hop check_url/validate_resolved re-validation, its own hops/max_redirects counter) needs requests' library-level redirect ceiling to NOT fire first -- confirmed by reading requests/sessions.py directly: resolve_redirects's while-loop checks 'if len(resp.history) >= self.max_redirects: raise TooManyRedirects' before ANY hop-specific logic runs, and this fires even in the yield_requests=True precomputation path used when allow_redirects=False, which itself never performs a live send (verified: it does a single next() call that yields once and stops, no network I/O) so raising the ceiling for this internal use doesn't reopen any auto-follow risk. Fixed by setting sess.max_redirects = max(max_redirects, 1) at the top of ssrf_request(), leaving ssrf_session()'s own standalone default (0) untouched for direct callers.
